Calc.methodIntro: Five points that separate a throwaway calculator from an instrument you use on every trade.

method.title: What other calculators do.
method.body: They treat risk as an isolated formula. You fill in eight fields, you click Calculate, you get a number disconnected from the rest. Drawdown never appears. Pip value is hidden. The page loads with three ad banners and a broker affiliate link.

method.title: What the Meridian Calculator does.
method.body: It treats risk as a system. Risk, position size, R-multiple, drawdown projected over fifteen consecutive losses — a single screen. No Calculate button: every value you change updates the result instantly.

method.title: What you won't find.
method.body: No ads. No broker affiliation. No forced sign-up. No aggressive email capture. No buy or sell signal. No profit promise. No euro amount tied to a named strategy.

method.title: What you'll find instead.
method.body: An instrument you use three seconds before every trade. A local memory of your preferences. A shareable URL that encodes your whole calculation. A method tied to the risk-management framework, free, with no email asked.

Calc.faqIntro: Eight short answers. If a question is missing, write to us: we'll add it.

faq.a: The calculation is instant. Every value you change updates the result without a click. The Calculate button is a leftover from 2010s banking forms. You don't need it.

faq.q: How does Meridian know my instrument's pip value?
faq.a: The tool uses each instrument's standard specs (contract size, pip size) combined with the entry price you enter. To convert to your account currency, indicative rates are applied — they can be refined in advanced mode in a future version.

1% is a widespread teaching reference, not a truth. The right value depends on your measured edge, your tolerable drawdown and your horizon. The Risk Management framework explains why 1% is arbitrary.

It's the cumulative loss if you string together N consecutive losses at your current risk. At 1% per trade, ten consecutive losses erase 9.56% of capital. The math is geometric, not linear. No classic calculator shows it.
Capital, currency and favorite instruments are stored in your local browser (localStorage). Nothing is sent to a Meridian server. You can clear everything by wiping the site's storage.

faq.q: Why doesn't Meridian show my broker?
faq.a: Meridian has no broker affiliation. Calculators that do lose their neutrality: the result is subtly skewed to nudge you into opening an account. Here, the result is just the calculation.

faq.q: What if I want to log my trades?
faq.a: Meridian Journal arrives later this year. This tool is the outpost: what you calculate before the trade, the Journal measures after.

faq.q: Does the tool work on mobile?
faq.a: Yes. Built mobile-first: inputs have a comfortable touch height, numbers stay readable without zoom, and the numeric keypad triggers automatically on price fields.
